title: Security & Privacy
lead: Privacy by architecture, plus the input-validation and hardening layers.
summary: MemPalace is designed with privacy-by-architecture: all data lives locally, no external APIs for core operations, zero phone-home. This architectural guarantee is reinforced by defense-in-depth input validation (sanitize_name/content), prompt contamination prevention (query_sanitizer), MCP stdio protection, symlink-attack rejection in export, shell hook hardening, and strict file permissions (0o600/0o700).

concepts.definition: The system physically cannot send data externally because it never leaves the local machine. No telemetry, no analytics, no phone-home. Core operations (mining, search, embedding, LLM calls) default to local-only; external providers require explicit user configuration.

Functions like sanitize_name(), sanitize_content(), and sanitize_kg_value() that enforce safe character sets, length bounds, null-byte rejection, lone-surrogate stripping, and path-traversal prevention at the API boundary.

A four-stage extraction pipeline in query_sanitizer.py that recovers user intent from queries contaminated by prepended system prompts, preventing retrieval failure (89.8% -> 1.0% without, ~70-89% with sanitizer).
Redirects stdout to stderr before heavy imports so transitive dependencies (like onnxruntime, telemetry libraries) that print to C-level stdout cannot break JSON-RPC parsing in Claude Desktop.
Defense-in-depth guard that refuses to follow symlinks during export or file I/O; uses O_NOFOLLOW on POSIX systems to atomically reject symlinks at open time, closing the TOCTOU window.
Config files, people maps, and exported directories are created with 0o600 (owner read/write only) or 0o700 (owner only) permissions, atomically via umask or os.open flags to prevent TOCTOU races.
The bash save hook parses JSON input safely without eval, validates transcript paths (suffix checks, .. rejection), sanitizes session IDs to alphanumerics, and logs parse failures to aid debugging.
Windows stdio reconfiguration to UTF-8 with per-stream error policies (strict on server, replace on CLI) and surrogateescape on stdin to survive malformed bytes without UnicodeDecodeError.
Rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes (file://, ftp://, etc.) in LLM_ENDPOINT to prevent misconfiguration from exfiltrating local files via a rogue endpoint.

symbols.name: sanitize_name()
symbols.role: Validates and sanitizes wing/room/entity names; blocks path traversal, null bytes, non-ASCII symbols; enforces 128-char max.

symbols.name: sanitize_content()
symbols.role: Validates drawer/diary content; rejects null bytes, enforces 100KB max; calls strip_lone_surrogates() for UTF-8 safety.

symbols.name: sanitize_kg_value()
symbols.role: Validates knowledge-graph entity names; more permissive than sanitize_name() (allows punctuation), still rejects null bytes and over-length.

symbols.name: strip_lone_surrogates()
symbols.role: Replaces lone UTF-16 surrogates (U+D800-U+DFFF) with U+FFFD to ensure legal UTF-8, preventing ChromaDB encode crashes (#1235).

symbols.name: sanitize_query()
symbols.role: Mitigates system-prompt contamination in search queries; returns clean query + metadata (was_sanitized, method, original/clean lengths).

symbols.name: _reject_symlink()
symbols.role: Pre-check that refuses to follow symlinks at export target; raises ValueError if path is a symlink.

symbols.name: _safe_open_for_write()
symbols.role: Opens files for writing with O_NOFOLLOW (POSIX) or pre-check (Windows) to prevent symlink following; files opened 0o600.

symbols.name: reconfigure_stdio_utf8_on_windows()
symbols.role: Reconfigures Windows stdio to UTF-8 with per-stream error policies; fixes ANSI codepage mojibake.

symbols.name: _validate_transcript_path()
symbols.role: Validates transcript paths: suffix check (.json/.jsonl), .. rejection, returns resolved Path or None.

symbols.name: _sanitize_session_id()
symbols.role: Sanitizes session IDs to alphanumerics + dash/underscore, preventing path traversal via hook input.

symbols.name: MempalaceConfig.init()
symbols.role: Creates ~/.mempalace directory with 0o700 and config.json with 0o600; restrictive permissions from the start.

symbols.name: LLMConfig
symbols.role: Resolves LLM endpoint config; validates scheme to http/https only, rejecting file:// and other protocols.

surprises.title: Lone Surrogate Issue Was Triggered by MCP Clients
surprises.detail: The _LONE_SURROGATE_RE pattern exists because Claude Desktop and other MCP clients occasionally relay lone UTF-16 surrogates when copying binary or corrupted data from the clipboard. This is not a user error - it's a platform quirk. Without strip_lone_surrogates(), ChromaDB crashes with -32000 (unexpected) when encoding, making memory operations silently fail. The fix is simple but essential.

surprises.title: Query Sanitizer Recovers 70-89% in Worst Case
surprises.detail: Issue #333 showed that without sanitization, system-prompt-contaminated queries drop to 1.0% retrieval (complete failure). With the four-stage sanitizer, worst-case (tail truncation fallback) is ~70-80%, and common cases (question extraction, tail sentence) hit 85-89%. This is not a perfect solution but a pragmatic mitigation: a searchable degradation beats silent failure.

surprises.title: MCP Stdio Redirection Uses File Descriptors, Not Just Python
surprises.detail: The mcp_server.py redirects stdout to stderr at both the Python level (sys.stdout = sys.stderr) and the file-descriptor level (os.dup2(2, 1)). This is necessary because transitive C libraries (onnxruntime, telemetry) print directly to fd 1 (C stdout), bypassing Python's sys.stdout. Skipping the fd-level redirect would still fail.

surprises.title: Bash 3.2 Compat Prevents Use of mapfile
surprises.detail: macOS ships bash 3.2.57 (frozen in 2006 at GPLv3 cutoff). mapfile and readarray builtins only arrived in bash 4.0 (2009). The save hook can't use them; instead it parses Python output with sed -n 'Np' to read individual lines into shell variables. On a stock macOS, mapfile would silently fail, causing every hook value to default and produce zero saves (#1440).

surprises.title: Transcript Path Validation Mirrors Between Shell and Python
surprises.detail: The shell hook (mempal_save_hook.sh:219-230) and the Python hooks_cli.py (_validate_transcript_path, line 124) both enforce the same checks: .json/.jsonl suffix only, no '..' traversal segments. This is defense-in-depth: the shell guards input to the Python mining commands, and Python validates separately so either layer can catch breakout attempts. Both use the same rejection logic.

designDecisions.decision: Privacy by architecture - data never leaves the machine by design
designDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md principle: 'Local-first, zero external API by default.' The entire system is built to run offline. Mining, search, embedding, and (optionally) LLM calls all default to local execution. No telemetry library is imported. This eliminates the largest class of privacy bugs: exfiltration cannot happen because the code path does not exist. External providers are opt-in only, requiring explicit env-var configuration.

designDecisions.decision: Sanitize at input boundaries, not at storage
designDecisions.rationale: All sanitizers (sanitize_name, sanitize_content, sanitize_kg_value) live in config.py and are called at the API boundary (MCP tool inputs, CLI args, hook scripts). This defense-in-depth approach ensures invalid data is rejected before it can be stored or used for any operation. It also means the miner, searcher, and storage layers can trust their inputs are valid.

designDecisions.decision: Query sanitizer uses heuristic recovery (4 stages), not cryptographic certainty
designDecisions.rationale: Perfect detection of system-prompt contamination is impossible (no adversary model). Instead, the system uses pragmatic heuristics: short queries are likely clean, questions (?) are likely real user intent, tail sentences are likely the actual query. Worst-case fallback is tail truncation. This trades perfect detection for survivable degradation: 70-89% recovery instead of 1.0% failure.

designDecisions.decision: Symlink rejection uses O_NOFOLLOW on POSIX, pre-check on Windows
designDecisions.rationale: POSIX has O_NOFOLLOW which closes the TOCTOU window atomically at open time. Windows does not, so pre-checks are necessary. Rather than using different code paths, the exporter uses both: pre-check always, plus O_NOFOLLOW when available. This keeps the logic simple and consistent.

designDecisions.decision: Hook scripts use Python inline for parsing, not bash eval
designDecisions.rationale: Shell escaping is error-prone. The save hook parses JSON with Python's json.load() and sanitizes individual fields with regex, avoiding eval entirely. The shell reads back the sanitized values using sed (bounded, deterministic). This limits the blast radius of any input parsing bugs to the Python inline script, not the entire hook.

stats.label: Query sanitizer stages
stats.value: 4 (passthrough, question extraction, tail sentence, tail truncation)

related.why: Privacy-by-architecture is a core design principle; security layers reinforce the local-only guarantee.
Hook scripts (mempal_save_hook.sh) implement hardened JSON parsing and path validation to safely ingest auto-save triggers.
MCP server uses input sanitizers at tool boundaries and query sanitizer for search contamination mitigation.
ChromaDB and SQLite storage backends receive sanitized, validated input before any write operation.
LLM endpoint configuration validates URL scheme (http/https only) to prevent file:// exfiltration.
Repair and migration operations respect the same input validation and file permission constraints.

searchDoc.title: Security & Privacy
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace is privacy-by-architecture: all data lives locally with no external APIs for core operations and zero phone-home, reinforced by defense-in-depth input validation, prompt-contamination mitigation, MCP stdio protection, symlink-attack rejection, hardened hooks, and strict file permissions.
searchDoc.body: MemPalace is privacy by architecture. All user data, including drawers, the knowledge graph, embeddings, and indices, lives in ~/.mempalace/palace and never leaves the local machine. Core memory operations such as mining, searching, and embedding run locally by default and require no cloud account or internet connectivity. External providers like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Ollama are supported only through explicit user configuration via env vars or config.json and are never enabled silently. No telemetry library is imported, which eliminates the entire class of unintended exfiltration bugs because the code path simply does not exist. This architectural guarantee is reinforced by several hardening layers. Input validation runs at every boundary through sanitizers in config.py. The sanitize_name function blocks path traversal using checks for dot-dot, forward slash, and backslash, rejects null bytes and non-ASCII symbol characters, and enforces a 128 character limit. The sanitize_content function rejects null bytes and enforces a 100KB ceiling. The sanitize_kg_value function is more permissive, allowing punctuation, but still rejects null bytes and over-length strings. All sanitizers call strip_lone_surrogates to replace lone UTF-16 surrogates with U+FFFD before encoding, preventing ChromaDB encode crashes from issue 1235. Those lone surrogates come from MCP clients like Claude Desktop relaying corrupted clipboard data, not from user error. Prompt contamination mitigation lives in query_sanitizer.py. When AI agents prepend long system prompts to search queries, retrieval collapses from 89.8 percent to 1.0 percent. A four-stage pipeline of passthrough, question extraction, tail-sentence extraction, and tail truncation recovers intent, with worst-case recovery around 70 to 80 percent and common cases at 85 to 89 percent. The MCP server protects stdio by redirecting stdout to stderr at both the Python and file-descriptor level before heavy imports, so transitive libraries like onnxruntime or PostHog telemetry cannot corrupt JSON-RPC. The exporter rejects symlinks using O_NOFOLLOW on POSIX, which fails atomically with ELOOP and closes the TOCTOU window, falling back to an islink pre-check on Windows. Config files use 0o600 and directories use 0o700, applied atomically via umask or os.open flags. The save hook parses JSON with Python rather than shell eval, sanitizes session IDs to alphanumerics, validates transcript paths to .json or .jsonl suffixes with dot-dot rejection, and avoids mapfile for bash 3.2 compatibility on macOS. LLM endpoint configuration validates that the URL scheme is http or https only, rejecting file:// to prevent local-file exfiltration.
